subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Placenta Praevia: Painless Bleeding and Double Setup

steps.tx: Implantation of the placenta over or near the internal os is **placenta praevia**. It causes painless, causeless, recurrent bright red bleeding in late pregnancy. Digital vaginal examination is forbidden until praevia is excluded by scan. Bleeding is typically revealed, painless and recurrent, each episode heavier, the pattern called causeless in textbooks.
steps.say: Placenta praevia implants over the os and causes painless recurrent bright bleeding.

steps.tx: Bleeding without pain, contractions or evident cause characterises **painless bleeding** of praevia. The uterus stays soft and the fetal heart usually remains normal. This contrasts sharply with the painful bleeding of abruption. Malpresentation is common because the placenta occupies the lower segment the head should enter.
steps.say: Painless bleeding with a soft uterus characterises praevia against painful abruption.

steps.tx: Slowing of the fetal heart after a bleed as the head compresses the placenta is the **Stallworthy sign**. It historically suggested posterior placenta praevia before ultrasound. Today transvaginal scanning gives the diagnosis safely and precisely. The sign is obsolete in scanned women, but the physiology, head compression slowing the heart, still appears in questions.
steps.say: The Stallworthy sign historically suggested posterior praevia before ultrasound diagnosis.

steps.tx: Examination in theatre with full caesarean readiness, historically used to feel the placenta, is the **double setup examination**. Ultrasound has made it nearly obsolete. It survives only where imaging is unavailable and delivery is imminent anyway. It required two theatre teams on standby, one for vaginal examination and one ready for instant caesarean.
steps.say: Double setup examination in theatre is now nearly obsolete thanks to ultrasound.

steps.tx: A **transvaginal ultrasound** probe sits safely in the vagina and measures the gap between placental edge and internal os to the millimetre. That edge-to-os distance, not a digital examination, now defines placenta praevia. Under two centimetres at thirty-six weeks usually commits the woman to caesarean delivery. Many low placentas appear to migrate upward as the lower segment stretches, so the measurement is repeated before deciding.
steps.say: Edge to os distance under two centimetres near term usually means caesarean delivery. Transvaginal scanning gives the diagnosis safely and precisely.

vis.alt: Transvaginal ultrasound image with digital calipers measuring the short distance between the placental edge and the internal cervical os.
vis.caption: Calipers on the transvaginal scan turn placenta praevia into a number, and an edge within two centimetres of the os near term plans caesarean birth. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Transvaginal ultrasound measures the distance from placental edge to os as the **edge to os distance**. Under two centimetres near term usually means caesarean delivery. Many low placentas migrate upward as the lower segment develops. An edge within zero to 20 millimetres of the os at 36 weeks usually means caesarean, while beyond 20 millimetres vaginal birth is reasonable.
steps.say: Edge to os distance under two centimetres near term usually means caesarean delivery.

steps.tx: Most low lying placentas at twenty weeks move clear by term through apparent **placental migration**. The lower segment stretching carries the edge away from the os. A follow up scan at thirty two to thirty six weeks decides the birth plan. True migration does not occur; the lower segment grows and trophoblast thins away from the poorly supplied lower uterus.
steps.say: Placental migration clears most low placentas by term as the lower segment stretches.

steps.tx: A low placenta over an old caesarean scar is two diagnoses conspiring. The **praevia accreta link** exists because scarred lower segment lacks the decidua that normally limits trophoblast invasion, so a praevia implanting there can grow into bladder and myometrium as accreta spectrum. Antenatal recognition changes everything: planned caesarean in a centre with blood, interventional radiology and urology standing by. The woman whose praevia covers a scar therefore earns accreta protocol imaging, not just a routine follow up scan for placental position.
steps.say: Placenta praevia over a caesarean scar risks accreta, needing planned delivery in a prepared centre.

vis.caption: Praevia accreta link. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Major praevia covering the os needs planned caesarean at thirty six to thirty seven weeks, termed **planned delivery timing**. Unstable bleeding at any gestation forces immediate delivery. Blood is cross matched and consent includes possible hysterectomy. Steroids for fetal lung maturity are given when planned delivery falls before 37 weeks.
steps.say: Major praevia delivers by planned caesarean at thirty six to thirty seven weeks.

steps.tx: Praevia over a previous caesarean scar strongly predicts abnormally adherent placenta, the **praevia accreta link**. This combination produces the most dangerous haemorrhage in modern obstetrics. Antenatal diagnosis and planned surgery in specialist centres save lives. Every praevia over a scar earns a dedicated accreta protocol scan between 28 and 32 weeks.
steps.say: Praevia over a caesarean scar predicts accreta and needs specialist planned surgery.

steps.tx: Speculum examination is safe and useful in antepartum haemorrhage to exclude local causes, termed **speculum assessment**. It reveals cervical lesions, polyps and the amount of bleeding. Only digital examination waits for scan exclusion of praevia. A gentle speculum can also take swabs and exclude vaginitis or cervicitis as the bleeding source.
steps.say: Speculum assessment is safe in antepartum bleeding while digital examination waits for scanning.
